literal: Those who lack basic resources, completely not renouncing, is death to salt and to sour gruel.
translation: For those who lack the basic resources of life, not renouncing domestic life completely is a death-blow to even their meager salt and sour gruel.
modern: அனுபவிக்கத்தக்க பொருள்கள் இல்லாதவர்கள், இல்லற வாழ்க்கையை முற்றிலும் துறந்துவிடாமல் இருப்பது, அவர்கள் உண்ணும் எளிய உப்பிற்கும் கஞ்சிக்கும் கூட எமனாக (அழிவாக) முடியும்.
explanation: This couplet describes the extreme misery of poverty in domestic life. The word 'துப்புரவு' refers to the basic resources or comforts of life, while 'துவர' means completely. When destitute people who lack even basic amenities refuse to completely renounce the householder's life, they struggle to survive. Their desperate attempt to maintain a household makes them consume even the cheapest, most basic food items like salt and sour gruel, thereby acting as a destroyer to these meager provisions. The poet uses the image of 'death' to show how poverty reduces a person to a state where even the simplest sustenance is exhausted.
